specification.problem: Exact synthesis of a single-qubit unitary U over the Clifford-cyclotomic gate set (Clifford + Rz(pi/n), n even), returning a gate word with the minimum number of pi/n z-rotations, and then building that word as a one-qubit circuit.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Tiny instance: n=4 (Clifford+T), one qubit, U given by explicit entries in Z[e^{i pi/4},1/2]. The classical synthesis output is a word in H,S,X,Rz(pi/n), which is built as a 1-qubit circuit with no ancilla, no measurement and no black box. Outside scope: the proof that the ring characterization fails for 100% of even n, the exact height-drop bound for general n, and the optimality proof for general n.

symbols.meaning: even positive integer defining the rotation angle pi/n
primitive 2n-th root of unity e^{i pi/n}
target single-qubit unitary with entries u_{ij}
Galois conjugation zeta_{2n} -> zeta_{2n}^k, k coprime to 2n
heuristic height proxy of the first column of U (log-norm of |u|^2 denominators); a candidate quantity, not the paper's definition
candidate move C1 Rz(pi/n) C2 with C1, C2 single-qubit Cliffords
number of pi/n rotations in the output word

equations.label: Rotation gate
equations.description: Standard Qiskit rz convention; for n=4 it equals T up to global phase.
equations.justification: Standard gate definition. The abstract only names a z-rotation by pi/n; the exact convention is assumed.
assumptions: Global phase is ignored in comparison

equations.label: Ring characterization
equations.description: Exactly synthesizable unitaries equal unitaries over the ring for n=4. The abstract says it fails for most even n.
equations.abstract_quote: For the Clifford+T case $n=4$ the group of exactly synthesizable unitaries was shown to be equal to the group of unitaries with entries over the ring $\mathbb{Z}[e^{i\frac{\pi}{n}},1/2]$.
equations.justification: Direct reading of the abstract claim for n=4.
assumptions: Phase factors absorbed in the ring

equations.label: Column unitarity in every conjugate
equations.description: Unitarity is preserved under Galois embeddings, since the identity is algebraic over the field.
equations.justification: Follows from U^dagger U = I holding in the field, with complex conjugation commuting with the Galois action in an abelian CM field. This is the sketch's step 1, not abstract-sourced.

equations.label: Height proxy (assumed)
equations.description: Least denominator exponent of the first column, used as a T-count proxy. Equals 0 iff the column is Clifford-like (monomial) in the intended setting.
equations.justification: The sketch proposes a least-denominator exponent from a norm. The exact definition is not in the abstract, so this is a placeholder.
assumptions: For n=4 this reduces to the known sde-based T-count

equations.label: Greedy descent step
equations.description: Pick the Clifford-conjugated rotation that lowers the height, and iterate until the residual is Clifford. m is the number of rotations.
equations.justification: The abstract claims an efficient algorithm that is optimal in rotation count. The greedy form with meet-in-the-middle search comes from the sketch and is not confirmed.
assumptions: Height drops by a bounded amount per rotation
The greedy choice attains the bound

registers.name: q
registers.role: Single data qubit carrying the synthesized word; no ancilla

specification.initial_state: |0> on q; the circuit is compared via its unitary or statevector to U up to global phase

steps.description: Fix n (n=4 in scope) and the explicit target U with cyclotomic entries; check unitarity and ring membership.
Compute the height of the first column and enumerate the finite set of moves C1 Rz(pi/n) C2 over Clifford coset representatives.
Greedily apply the height-lowering move, record it, and repeat until the height is 0. Fail if no move lowers the height (non-synthesizable).

Fix the final Clifford residual by matching it to one of the 24 Clifford classes up to phase, and emit the word in h,s,x,rz gates in time order. Reverse the order of the recorded product when building, since the product is written right-to-left.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical synthesis search gives the gate word. The word is compared to U up to global phase. Rotation count m is reported.
assumptions: Smallest useful construction: n=4, one qubit, explicit U
Gate set is H, S, X, Rz(pi/n)
Search over Clifford cosets is finite, 24 classes up to phase
The Galois-norm height is a valid lower bound on m, taken from the sketch and unverified
missing_information: Exact definition of the height and of the per-rotation drop for general n
The paper's actual algorithm; the abstract gives no equations for it
Criterion for exact synthesizability for n other than 4
